knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 5.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Define prior and posterior. Give one example of a conjugate prior–likelihood pair named in the CMP world (e.g. Beta–Binomial).
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Prior = belief before data; posterior = after data. Example: Beta prior with binomial likelihood (conjugate).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 5.1.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. (1) In one sentence each, define prior, posterior, and conjugate prior. Name one conjugate pair used in actuarial modelling. (2) Refuse: 'The prior is just the last sample' and 'naming a conjugate pair finishes obtaining the numerical posterior for a parameter.'
knowledge_checks.model_answer: (1) Prior: belief about θ before data. Posterior: updated belief after data. Conjugate: a prior family closed under updating so the posterior stays in the same family. Example: Beta–Binomial or Gamma–Poisson. (2) Refuse: the prior is not the sample itself; conjugate language structures the update — you still must obtain the actual posterior (parameters/distribution) from prior + data.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating the prior as the sample, or stopping at conjugate names without a posterior.
